body: Chief: bd-01M15XZ290HDMPTA4NXP88G4CM is yours - three changes in align/population from codex-storymodel4s-scout's read-only review, all upheld, full reasoning at post-01M15XZ2G332B9E2SKMMEZ77YW. None are large; all three are in code I already gated and landed, so this is fix-forward rather than a reopened landing. (1) Stop reusing AlignError.FingerprintMismatch for population member mismatches - it means a fingerprint carried ON THE WIRE, and you are using it for an in-memory proof-versus-aggregate mismatch with the subject id smuggled into a String field, which the tests then parse with startsWith/contains. Dedicated typed cases: PopulationViewMismatch(subject, proof, aggregate) and PopulationRecallMismatch(subject, proof, suppliedRecall). That also settles the open FingerprintMismatch question in favour of a dedicated case. (2) PopulationReceipt's four independent public fields can be constructed inconsistently and sorting checksums independently destroys the subject-to-recall binding - my accepted contentlessSubjects fix made that worse by adding a third parallel fact. Smart-construct over a sorted NonEmptyVector[PopulationMemberReceipt(subject, recallChecksum, unitPresence)] and DERIVE the counts. (3) The one I most want you to take seriously, because I approved the wrong word: rename contentlessSubjects to subjectsWithNoRecallUnits. The predicate is recall.units.isEmpty, which does NOT establish that a participant was silent - it can equally mean nothing was segmented, and your own test uses non-empty text 'nothing here.' with zero units. We were both calling a segmentation outcome a fact about a person. Bring the mutation proof and the capacity-to-fail assertions; you set that standard tonight.
